summary: The study investigates ZnS thin films grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) from anhydrous zinc acetate and hydrogen sulphide at 290-330°C. The films exhibit varying crystallite sizes and microstrain, with the crystallite sizes depending on the film thickness. The results show differences in microstructural parameters compared to films grown from zinc chloride and electron beam evaporation (EBE).
evidence: The films were grown from anhydrous zinc acetate and hydrogen sulphide by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at 290-330°C. The average crystallite sizes are 40-80 nm, depending on the film thickness. The values are more than one-half of those observed earlier for ZnS thin films grown by ALE from zinc chloride and hydrogen sulphide and two to three times those found in the films grown by electron beam evaporation (EBE). The average magnitude of the microstrain in the films grown by ALE from zinc acetate was found to be (1-2) x 10^-3.
